title: One-step configuration code test
statement: Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine, $x$ a Boolean input word, and $S$ a natural number. Suppose $N$ uses at most $sp(|x|)$ space on every choice word for some function $sp$, and $sp(|x|)\le S$. If $C$ is reachable from the initial configuration of $N$ on $x$, then for every natural number $c'$, the Boolean indicator of the one-step language on the encoding of $x$, the code of $C$ with window size $S$, the number $c'$, and $S$ equals true exactly when $c'$ is the code, with window size $S$, of one of the two configurations obtained from $C$ by a step under a choice bit.
hypotheses_covered: N uses at most sp(|x|) space on every choice word
configuration C is reachable from the initial configuration on x
